- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 periods later.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward historical mean (last 10–15 days) by 1–2% per period.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a spike, model often fails to adjust — apply a “sentiment lag” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.33 within 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 2 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive — apply a “horizon bias” correction: subtract 1–2% from first 5 forecasts if sentiment >0.50.
